{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Indonesia|Cuisine of Indonesia]]

'''Lapis legit''' (Dutch: ''spekkoek'') is a spice-flavored multilayered cake. A legacy of Dutch occupation in Indonesia, the cake is enjoyed during Eid ul-Fitr and Christmas celebrations. In the Netherlands, the sliced cake is served as dessert in ''Rijsttafel'' (Indonesian rice table).

The cake has a firm texture similar to [[Cookbook:Baumkuchen|baumkuchen]], but without a chocolate or sugar shell. The cake requires much patience to bake. Each layer of the cake is made by pouring a small amount of batter from a cup into the baking tin, then putting the tin into the oven until the layer has become golden from the heat. The tin is then removed from the oven and the process is repeated until all the layers have been built up. Baking the cake in a gas oven gives a better aroma than using an electric oven, but a Dutch oven with a charcoal fire on top of the lid produces the best result.

If cloves or cardamom seeds are difficult to find, use spekkoek powder as a replacement. Milling and mixing the spices before baking produces a cake with an excellent aroma. 

==Ingredients==
* 10 whole [[Cookbook:Clove|cloves]], ground
* 10 [[Cookbook:Cardamom|cardamom]] seeds, ground
* 2 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Nutmeg|nutmeg]] powder
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] powder
* 1 teaspoon [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]] powder
* 10 [[Cookbook:Egg Yolk|egg yolks]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Egg White|egg whites]]
* 125 g [[Cookbook:Castor sugar|castor sugar]]
* 195 g sweetened [[Cookbook:Condensed milk|condensed milk]]
* 500 g [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 125 g cake [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]]

==Procedure==
# Mix and sift cloves, cardamom, nutmeg, and cinnamon.
# [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] butter until smooth and creamy.
# [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] egg yolks with sugar until fluffy.
# Whip egg whites in separate mixing bowl until fluffy, then mix with egg yolks.
# Combine the spices, condensed milk, flour, and butter.
# Grease a [[Cookbook:Cake Pan|cake pan]].
# Using a small cup, spread 30–35 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] batter into the pan to make a layer.
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in preheated 350°F [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]], heated from the top, until golden (4–5 minutes).
# Remove from oven, [[Cookbook:Brush|brush]] with butter for flavoring, and top with another 30–35 ml batter to make another layer.
# Repeat the baking and layering to make around 30–40 layers.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Adding to the complexity of the baking process, some cake shops add dried [[Cookbook:Plum|plums]] (prunes) inside and on top of the cake.
